name: Mira050
description: ams OSRAM Mira050 — 1/7" 0.5 MP NIR-enhanced global shutter, mono 8/10/10-HS/12-bit, MIPI CSI-2 D-PHY 1-lane up to 1.5 Gbit/s, max 200 fps @ 0.5 MP in 10-HS. Verified against DS000743 v9-01 (2025-Sep) and ams-OSRAM RPi4 driver mira050.inl (release v2024-07-1).
guide:
Mira050 quick guide (per DS000743 v9-01)
=========================================

- 576x768 active pixels (CSP) / 600x800 (bare die), 2.79 µm pitch, BSI global shutter.
- 8 / 10 / 10-HS / 12-bit RAW, max 200 fps @ 0.5 MP in 10-HS mode (sec. 1.1).
- MIPI CSI-2 v1.3 + D-PHY v1.2, 1 data + 1 clock lane, up to 1.5 Gbit/s/lane.
- CCI (sec. 6.4): 16-bit register address, 8-bit data. I2C slave 011011Xb, X from CCI_ADDRESS pin.
- Default ams driver mode: 576x768 @ 50 fps, 12-bit, 1-lane MIPI @ 1.5 Gbit/s.
- CLK_IN (sec. 6.3): 12-64 MHz (excluding 20-24 MHz). ams driver uses 24 MHz.

CRITICAL — Banking (sec. 6.4, driver lines 104, 3201-3211)
----------------------------------------------------------
Unlike the Mira220, the Mira050 partitions its low-address registers (0x00xx, 0x01xx)
into multiple BANKS. Some addresses (notably 0x001D) carry different meaning in bank 0
vs bank 1. ALWAYS write BANK_SEL (0xE000) to the required bank before touching any
register tagged with a `bank` field in this profile. Registers tagged `bank: null`
(or without a bank field) are bank-independent (0xE0xx, 0x20xx, 0x40xx).

The ams driver convention (used at run-time):
  - bank 0: TRIG_SYNC_DELAY (0x001A), DMUX0_SEL (0x00F3)
  - bank 1: EN_TRIG_ILLUM (0x001C), ILLUM_WIDTH/DELAY (0x0019, 0x0016),
            EN_TRIG_SYNC and TRIG_SYNC_ON_REQ_1 (both 0x001D in bank 1 per runtime trace)
  - bank-independent: everything in 0xE0xx, 0x20xx, 0x40xx

Key register groups
-------------------
  0xE000        BANK_SEL          0 or 1, prerequisite for bank-scoped writes.
  0xE004        RW_CONTEXT        A/B context selector (sec. 6.4.4).
  0x000A        CMD_REQ_1         Rising edge -> REQ_EXP (sec. 6.9).
  0x000C        CMD_HALT_BLOCK    Rising edge -> stop Streaming -> IDLE.
  0x0008..000B  TARGET_FRAME_TIME 32-bit µs, frame period (Triggered Internal / Streaming).
  0x000E..0011  EXP_TIME_L        32-bit µs, primary exposure.
  0x0012..0015  EXP_TIME_S        32-bit µs, dark exposure (BLC mode only).
  0x0016..0018  ILLUM_DELAY       24-bit, 20 LSB valid; TRIG_ILLUM vs exposure offset.
  0x0019..001B  ILLUM_WIDTH       24-bit, TRIG_ILLUM high time.
  0x001C        EN_TRIG_ILLUM     bit[0] enable TRIG_ILLUM output (bank 1).
  0x001D        EN_TRIG_SYNC / TRIG_SYNC_ON_REQ_1 (bank 1).
  0x001A        TRIG_SYNC_DELAY   slave-sync delay (bank 0).
  0x0024        GDIG_AMP          digital gain amp (datasheet sec. 5.2.3).
  0x0056..0057  DELTA_TEST_IMG    2D gradient step for test pattern mode 0x02.
  0x0060..0061  TRAINING_WORD     fixed value for test pattern mode 0x01.
  0x0062        TEST_PATTERN      0=off, 1=fixed, 2=2D gradient.
  0x0064..006F  OTP_*             OTP memory access (sec. 5.10).
  0x0193..0194  OFFSET_CLIPPING   black-level offset clip (16-bit).
  0x01F0/01F3   BIAS_RG_ADCGAIN / BIAS_RG_MULT  analog-gain LUT entries.
  0x207C        PLL_LOCKED        bit[0] = 1 when PLL locked (read-only).
  0x209A        CSI2_TX_HS_ACTIVE D-PHY data lane in HS state (read-only).
  0x4002        CURRENT_ACTIVE_CONTEXT  reads back live A/B context.

Sensor Control Modes (sec. 6.8)
-------------------------------
  Full External, Triggered Internal, Background Light Cancellation, Streaming.
  BLC mode pairs EXP_TIME_L (illuminated) with EXP_TIME_S (dark) and performs
  on-chip subtraction (sec. 6.8.4, fig. 24-25). Unique to the Mira050 family.

Bring-up sequence per mode
--------------------------
  Each acquisition mode (e.g. 576x768_50fps_12b_1lane) requires uploading a
  pre-soft-reset register table (~640 writes, ams driver lines 308-953 for 12-bit),
  then a soft reset, then a post-soft-reset table (~3 writes). These bulk uploads
  are part of the .cfg file, not editable per-register from the GUI.

Notes
-----
- I2C addresses 0x0A (µC), 0x2D (PMIC), 0x53 (LED driver) belong to the RPi4 sensor
  board companion chips, NOT to the Mira050 itself. Irrelevant for the FX3 EVK.
- Analog gain in 12-bit Default mode is discrete (x1, x2, x4), loaded from the
  three partial_analog_gain_xN_12bit[] tables in the ams driver. Manual editing
  of GDIG_AMP / BIAS_RG_ADCGAIN / BIAS_RG_MULT requires reproducing a full LUT row.
- Color filter info (RGB / RGB-IR): the GUI is configured mono-only; for RGB variants
  the on-chip Bayer pattern is BG/GR for RGB and a 4x4 RGB-IR pattern (sec. 8).

tabs.controls: The cfg exposes Framerate and Exp(us) via the SDK. Analog gain is discrete (x1/x2/x4 in 12-bit Default) loaded from on-chip LUT; manual override via GDIG_AMP/BIAS_RG_* is possible but must reproduce a full LUT row.
tabs.registers: REMEMBER the BANK_SEL prerequisite for bank-scoped registers (0x001C, 0x001D, 0x0019, 0x0016, 0x001A, 0x00F3 and others). Check the bank field in each register entry and write BANK_SEL = bank before the I2C transaction.
tabs.advanced: 1-lane MIPI @ 1.5 Gbit/s data rate. Re-tune FX3 transfer size if changing bit depth (8b VGA reaches ~250 fps and stresses USB throughput differently than 12b).

registers.name: Bank select
registers.desc: BANK_SEL — partitions the low-address register space
registers.help:
Mira050-specific. Selects which bank of registers is addressed when writing to the 0x00xx/0x01xx ranges. Bank 0 after reset.

The Mira220 has no such banking, which is why this register has no equivalent in the Mira220 profile.

Prerequisite for every bank-scoped write in this profile. If a register entry has "bank": 1, write BANK_SEL = 1 first, then perform the I2C transaction, then optionally restore BANK_SEL = 0.

registers.name: Active context (A / B)
registers.desc: RW_CONTEXT — selects which of the two register contexts receives writes
registers.help:
Per DS000743 sec. 6.4.4. The Mira050 keeps two parallel sets of context-switchable registers (exposure, ROI, gain, illumination-trigger enable, ...). Writes hit the context selected here.

By default the active-context handover is synchronised to the next frame readout, so staging configuration in the inactive context does not disturb the current acquisition.

Readback of the live context is at 0x4002 (CURRENT_ACTIVE_CONTEXT).

registers.name: Request exposure (CMD_REQ_1)
registers.desc: CMD_REQ_1 [0] — rising edge triggers REQ_EXP
registers.help:
Software equivalent of the REQ_1 pin. A rising edge on bit 0 triggers a REQ_EXP command, which starts an exposure (Full External mode) or a finite sequence (Triggered Internal / Background Light Cancellation / Streaming modes).

In single-pin control, a falling edge on this bit additionally triggers REQ_FRAME (datasheet sec. 6.8.1).

registers.name: Halt streaming (CMD_HALT_BLOCK)
registers.desc: CMD_HALT_BLOCK [0] — exit Streaming mode
registers.help: Rising edge on bit 0 finishes the current frame readout and moves the sensor back to IDLE. This is the only documented way to exit Streaming mode without an external reset (datasheet sec. 6.9).

registers.name: Target frame time (us)
registers.desc: TARGET_FRAME_TIME (32-bit, µs) — frame period in Triggered Internal / BLC / Streaming
registers.help:
Inter-frame period in microseconds. 32-bit big-endian register (ams driver write_be32, line 3696). Ignored in Full External mode.

For maximum frame rate, set this equal to glob_time + readout_time. The driver-derived MIN_VBLANK is 15900 (60 fps) or 7560 (120 fps) — use those as practical lower bounds when manually computing.

WARNING: shares address 0x000A with CMD_REQ_1 in single-byte writes. The driver always uses a 4-byte big-endian write_be32, which atomically covers 0x0008..0x000B.

registers.name: Exposure long / primary (us)
registers.desc: EXP_TIME_L (32-bit, µs) — primary / illuminated exposure
registers.help:
Primary exposure time in microseconds. 32-bit big-endian write (ams driver write_be32, line 3669).

Driver-computed min is ~5 µs at 1.5 Gbit/s 12-bit, max capped at 1 s. Default exposure is 1000 µs.

In Background Light Cancellation mode (sec. 6.8.4) this is the ILLUMINATED exposure; the dark exposure uses EXP_TIME_S (0x0012).

registers.name: Exposure short / dark (us, BLC mode)
registers.desc: EXP_TIME_S (32-bit, µs) — dark exposure in BLC mode
registers.help:
Only used in Background Light Cancellation mode (datasheet sec. 6.8.4 / fig. 24). Programs the exposure of the first (no-illumination) capture.

The on-chip subtraction emits the difference image; a single MIPI readout per BLC frame is generated.

In all other modes, this register is unused.

registers.name: Enable TRIG_ILLUM output
registers.desc: EN_TRIG_ILLUM [0] — master enable for TRIG_ILLUM pad (bank 1)
registers.help:
Master enable for the TRIG_ILLUM output pin, which drives an external NIR illuminator in sync with the pixel exposure (datasheet sec. 5.11). Width programmed at 0x0019 (ILLUM_WIDTH), delay at 0x0016 (ILLUM_DELAY).

The ams driver writes this with BANK_SEL = 1 (line 3208) before the I2C transaction (line 3248).

registers.name: Illumination width
registers.desc: ILLUM_WIDTH (24-bit) — high time of TRIG_ILLUM
registers.help:
High time of the TRIG_ILLUM pulse, all 24 bits valid (ams driver comment, line 3271).

Driver default = EXP_TIME × DATA_RATE / 8. The trigger is synchronised to the actual pixel exposure, so sensor-side latency between request and exposure start is auto-compensated by the on-chip sequencer (datasheet fig. 4).

Address 0x001A is shared with TRIG_SYNC_DELAY in bank 0 — make sure BANK_SEL = 1 before this write.

registers.name: Illumination delay
registers.desc: ILLUM_DELAY (24-bit, [19:0] valid) — TRIG_ILLUM rising edge vs exposure start
registers.help:
Programmable delay between the TRIG_ILLUM rising edge and the start of pixel exposure. Only bits [19:0] of the 24-bit field are valid (ams driver comment, line 3280) — upper 4 bits are reserved.

Positive, negative or zero delay are supported (datasheet sec. 5.11 fig. 4). Driver default = 1 << 19.

registers.name: Enable TRIG_SYNC / tie REQ_1 to TRIG_SYNC
registers.desc: EN_TRIG_SYNC / TRIG_SYNC_ON_REQ_1 [0] — slave-sync enable (bank 1)
registers.help:
Single physical bit at 0x001D in bank 1, referenced by the ams driver under two semantic names (EN_TRIG_SYNC at line 3265, TRIG_SYNC_ON_REQ_1 at line 3256) — the driver writes the same value to the same register in both calls. Documenting both names for cross-reference with driver source.

When 1, the TRIG_SYNC output is enabled and follows the REQ_1 edge; used to slave a second sensor in a stereo setup (TRIG_SYNC pin not bonded on CSP package).

NOTE: the #define MIRA050_TRIG_SYNC_ON_REQ_1 in the driver header has a stale "// bank 0" comment that contradicts the runtime BANK_SEL = 1 at lines 3208 / 3265. We follow the runtime behaviour as authoritative.

registers.name: TRIG_SYNC delay
registers.desc: TRIG_SYNC_DELAY (bank 0) — slave-sync output delay
registers.help:
Programmable delay on the TRIG_SYNC output pad. Bank-0 address — make sure BANK_SEL = 0 before writing.

Note: shares its byte addresses with the middle bytes of ILLUM_WIDTH in bank 1. Banking is the only thing that disambiguates them.

registers.name: DMUX0 output select
registers.desc: DMUX0_SEL — internal signal routed to DMUX0 test pad (bank 0)
registers.help: Selects which internal signal is muxed to the DMUX0 test pad. The ams driver uses values 39 (manual illumination) and 40 (auto / sync-tied).

registers.name: Digital gain amplifier
registers.desc: GDIG_AMP — digital gain control
registers.help:
Digital gain. Datasheet documents a 1/16x step from 1x to 16x in 8/10/10-HS/12-bit modes (sec. 5.2.3). Exact register encoding is documented in product description PD001051 (not in the public datasheet) — ams driver loads this together with the per-mode analog-gain LUT entry.

Do not edit standalone unless reproducing a full LUT row from partial_analog_gain_xN_12bit[] in the ams driver.

registers.name: Bias ADC gain (analog gain LUT)
registers.desc: BIAS_RG_ADCGAIN — analog gain ADC bias (LUT entry)
registers.help: Part of the analog-gain LUT. The ams driver loads it from the partial_analog_gain_x{1,2,4}_12bit tables together with BIAS_RG_MULT and GDIG_AMP. Do not edit manually unless you are reproducing one of those LUT entries.

registers.name: Bias multiplier (analog gain LUT)
registers.desc: BIAS_RG_MULT — analog gain multiplier bias (LUT entry)
registers.help: Companion to BIAS_RG_ADCGAIN in the analog-gain LUT. See note on the BIAS_RG_ADCGAIN entry.

registers.name: Offset clipping
registers.desc: OFFSET_CLIPPING (16-bit) — black-level offset clipping
registers.help: 16-bit big-endian register controlling the offset subtracted before output (ams driver write_be16, lines 3933 / 3996). Loaded as part of the per-mode pre-soft-reset sequence.

registers.name: Test pattern mode
registers.desc: TEST_PATTERN — replaces pixel data with synthetic pattern
registers.help:
Useful for MIPI link integrity testing and for validating the host-side ISP without a scene.

  0x00  Disabled (normal pixel data)
  0x01  Fixed value taken from TRAINING_WORD (0x0060/0x0061)
  0x02  2D gradient with per-pixel step from DELTA_TEST_IMG (0x0056/0x0057)

registers.name: Training word
registers.desc: TRAINING_WORD (16-bit) — fixed value for test pattern mode 0x01
registers.help: Pixel value emitted by every pixel when TEST_PATTERN = 0x01.

registers.name: 2D gradient step
registers.desc: DELTA_TEST_IMG (16-bit) — per-pixel increment for 2D gradient
registers.help: Per-pixel increment used by test-pattern mode 0x02.

registers.name: OTP command
registers.desc: OTP_COMMAND — OTP operation selector

registers.name: OTP address
registers.desc: OTP_ADDR — OTP word address

registers.name: OTP start
registers.desc: OTP_START [0] — rising edge starts the OTP transaction
registers.help: Write 1, then 0, to launch the OTP operation specified by OTP_COMMAND / OTP_ADDR. Poll OTP_BUSY (0x0065) until 0, then read OTP_DOUT (0x006C..0x006F).

registers.name: OTP busy
registers.desc: OTP_BUSY [0] — 1 while OTP transaction in flight (read-only)
registers.help: Read-only status. The 8 kbit OTP holds the unique device ID and ams calibration data (datasheet sec. 5.10).

registers.name: OTP data out
registers.desc: OTP_DOUT (32-bit, big-endian read) — OTP read register
registers.help: Read-only. The ams driver reads 4 consecutive bytes starting at 0x006C with read_be32 (line 3055). Available after OTP_BUSY clears.

registers.name: PLL locked
registers.desc: PLL_LOCKED [0] — set when the on-chip PLL has locked
registers.help: Poll after the PLL enable write during power-up; the sensor cannot stream until this reads 1 (datasheet sec. 6.2.1 step 7). Bank-independent.

registers.name: CSI-2 TX HS active
registers.desc: CSI2_TX_HS_ACTIVE [0] — D-PHY data lane in high-speed state
registers.help: Read-only. 1 = data lane currently in HS mode (i.e. transmitting a packet burst), 0 = LP / ULPS. Useful for diagnosing host receiver issues. Bank-independent.

registers.name: Current active context
registers.desc: CURRENT_ACTIVE_CONTEXT [0] — live A/B context the sequencer is using
registers.help: Read-only mirror of which of the two register contexts (A = 0, B = 1) is currently in use by the sequencer. Use this to verify a context switch has landed before reusing the previous context for staging the next configuration. Bank-independent.
